project.name: CenEkathon AI-readiness app
project.summary: A web app that turns labour-market vacancy data and a company's own AI usage into an AI-readiness score and three ranked actions. A Claude-powered agent answers questions on top of DuckDB tables built from the hackathon vacancy data.

nodes.label: Web app
nodes.summary: What people see in the browser: the chat and the dashboard.

nodes.label: Chat pages
nodes.summary: Next.js pages where a person asks a question and reads the answer.

nodes.label: Dashboard
nodes.summary: Vite-built dashboard that shows scores and trends.

nodes.label: Chat API
nodes.summary: The HTTP endpoints the web app calls. They pass questions on to the backend.

nodes.label: Analysis backend
nodes.summary: Server that answers questions with the agent, the router and the readiness score, and reads the vacancy and internal tables.

nodes.label: Slack and MCP bots
nodes.summary: Optional entry points: a Slack bot and an MCP server that give other tools access to the same answers.

nodes.label: DuckDB store
nodes.summary: Normalises the yearly vacancy files and builds the DuckDB database the backend queries.

nodes.label: Data preparation
nodes.summary: Scripts that inspect the hackathon Parquet files, clean them, and collect public datasets. They are run by hand, not by the app.

nodes.label: Synthetic bank data
nodes.summary: Made-up internal data for Northwind Bank: headcount, AI usage, learning and recruiting. Every row is marked synthetic.

nodes.label: Deploy and checks
nodes.summary: Docker, Compose, Vercel config and the shell checks that run in the project.

nodes.label: Claude API
nodes.summary: The language model that writes answers and labels.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.summary: The workspace the Slack bot talks in.

nodes.label: Jev decision API
nodes.summary: TypeSafe's decision model. It picks one option from a list and returns a probability for each.

nodes.label: Public data sources
nodes.summary: Official datasets the preparation scripts download: ESCO, GLEIF, Eurostat, ONS, CBS, Statbel and Hugging Face.

nodes.label: DuckDB
nodes.summary: The embedded database engine the store and the backend use.

issues.title: None of .’s endpoints check who is calling
issues.detail: 3 endpoints answer anyone who knows the address, with no login check in the code. That's fine only if this server is private (for example behind a company network or a gateway that checks logins); otherwise anyone could read or change its data.
issues.fix:
Review access control in .. None of these endpoints verify the caller in code:
- POST /api/chat — src/app/api/chat/route.ts:1
- GET /api/documents/[id] — src/app/api/documents/[id]/route.ts:1
- GET /api/overview — src/app/api/overview/route.ts:1

First tell me in plain words whether this server is reachable from the internet and whether anything in front of it (gateway, network rules) checks logins. If it is public, propose the smallest safe way to require login for the data-changing endpoints (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) first, show me the plan, and wait for my OK before changing code.
